standard.title: Create short written texts
standard.description: create and participate in shared editing of short written texts to record and report ideas and events using some learnt vocabulary, basic sentence boundary punctuation and spelling some consonant–vowel–consonant words correctly
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have beginning letter-sound and word knowledge (AC9EFLY09–15). They have not yet been asked to compose and edit connected written text — integrating spelling, vocabulary, punctuation and ideas into a coherent short text.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can create short written texts to record or report ideas and events — using learnt vocabulary, CVC spelling and basic sentence punctuation — and can participate in shared editing to improve a text.

nodes.label: Writing communicates an idea
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can produce a short text (drawing and/or beginning writing) that communicates one idea or event.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a text with at least one written word or sentence (and/or drawing) that communicates an idea.
nodes.typical_width: Create short written texts using beginning writing knowledge, sound-letter relationships and known words; combine writing and drawing to communicate personal responses to ideas and events.
wider: Create texts for different purposes — recording an event, responding to a story, reporting an observation — and compare how purpose affects what is written
Create multimodal texts using digital tools that combine writing and images
success_criteria: Student produces a text that communicates a recognisable idea or event.
Student's text includes at least one written word alongside or within a drawing.

nodes.label: CVC spelling, vocabulary and punctuation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply CVC spelling, use some learnt vocabulary, and include a capital letter at the sentence start and a full stop at the end.
nodes.minimum_width: Write at least one sentence with a capital letter at the start and a full stop at the end, spelling at least one CVC word correctly.
nodes.typical_width: Use learnt vocabulary in writing; spell some CVC words correctly; apply basic sentence boundary punctuation (capital letter and full stop); demonstrate growing control of these conventions in short texts.
wider: Write short texts across different topics, applying vocabulary and spelling knowledge to new content
Experiment with question marks and exclamation marks in appropriate writing contexts
Use topic-specific vocabulary from cross-curricular learning in written texts
nodes.hinge_reason: Without these conventions being at least partially established, students cannot productively participate in shared editing in Node 3 — they need something to read back and review, and the editing process presupposes that conventions have been attempted.

response_modes.reason: CVC spelling accuracy and sentence punctuation conventions are precision skills — errors cascade into illegible or misleading texts. Practice across multiple writing tasks consolidates these as reliable conventions rather than occasional correct applications.

success_criteria: Student uses a capital letter at the start of a sentence and a full stop at the end.
Student spells at least one CVC word correctly without prompting.
Student uses at least one learnt vocabulary word accurately in context.

nodes.label: Reading back and shared editing
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can 'read' their own text back and participate in shared editing — identifying at least one thing to change or correct.
nodes.minimum_width: Read their own text back to an experienced writer and identify at least one capital letter at a sentence start.
nodes.typical_width: Read own texts back; participate in shared editing by identifying capital letters at sentence beginnings; respond to feedback from an experienced writer and make at least one improvement.
wider: Participate in shared editing with a focus on a chosen feature — punctuation, vocabulary, spelling — applying what is learned to future writing
Read back texts from multiple writing events and identify growth over time
Contribute to editing of a class-shared text, justifying each editing decision

response_modes.reason: Reading back and editing requires coordinating all previously learned conventions — punctuation, spelling, vocabulary — as a self-monitoring and improvement process. The act of authoring and reviewing one's own text integrates the learning.

success_criteria: Student can read their own text back and identify what it says.
Student can participate in shared editing and identify at least one feature to change.
Student makes at least one improvement following feedback.
